inputs: SP 800-38A Appendix F.2 AES-128-CBC four-block vector
expected: All four ciphertext blocks match the NIST values; decryption with the same IV recovers all four plaintext blocks
limitations: One official four-block case; it checks the CBC formula and vector, not protocol behavior.

inputs: Fixed AES-128 key and first plaintext block under different IVs, including a one-bit IV change
expected: Different IVs change the first ciphertext block; the same IV reproduces it; flipping an IV bit flips the same bit in P1 only
limitations: Structural demonstration of IV influence; it does not implement a chosen-plaintext attack.

inputs: Four-block AES-128-CBC ciphertext with one bit flipped in C2
expected: P2 is corrupted, the same bit of P3 flips, and P1 and P4 are unchanged
limitations: Malleability demonstration on fixed data; not a complete oracle attack.

inputs: Four-block plaintext encrypted twice under the same key and IV, changing only P2
expected: C1 is unchanged; C2, C3 and C4 all change because encryption chaining propagates the change
limitations: Shows encryption chaining, not decryption error propagation.

inputs: 20-byte and 16-byte plaintexts padded with the CMS/PKCS#7 rule for a 16-byte block
expected: 20 bytes become 32 with twelve 0x0c bytes; 16 bytes become 32 with sixteen 0x10 bytes; unpadding restores both
limitations: Padding mechanics only; it does not test oracle behavior or every malformed padding case.

inputs: Birthday collision probability for 64-bit ciphertext blocks at 2^32 and 2^32.5 blocks
expected: Probability is about 39.3% at 2^32 blocks and about 63.2% at 2^32.5 blocks
limitations: Birthday arithmetic only; 2^32 blocks equal 32 GiB at 8 bytes per block.
